text: Attention Is All You Need. The Transformer architecture, based solely on attention mechanisms without recurrence or convolutions, achieves superior results on machine translation. Self-attention allows each position in the encoder to attend to all positions in the encoder. Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. The Transformer achieves 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German translation.
title: Attention Is All You Need

text: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention. FlashAttention is an IO-aware exact attention algorithm that uses tiling to reduce memory reads and writes between GPU HBM and on-chip SRAM. FlashAttention trains Transformers 2-4x faster than baselines and uses 5-20x less memory with no approximation. It makes exact attention feasible on sequences of 64K tokens on a single A100 GPU.
title: FlashAttention: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Attention

text: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer. Longformer uses a combination of windowed local-context self-attention and global attention that scales linearly with sequence length, making it easy to process documents of thousands of tokens. It achieves state-of-the-art results on character-level language modeling and several long document NLP tasks.
title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer

text: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers. BERT pre-trains deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers using Masked Language Modeling and Next Sentence Prediction. Fine-tuned BERT achieves state-of-the-art on eleven NLP tasks including SQuAD and GLUE.
title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers

text: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach. RoBERTa shows BERT was significantly undertrained. Key improvements include training longer with bigger batches on more data, removing Next Sentence Prediction, training on longer sequences, and dynamically changing masking patterns. RoBERTa matches or exceeds XLNet on all benchmarks.
title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

text: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning. ALBERT uses factorized embedding parameterization and cross-layer parameter sharing to reduce memory consumption and increase BERT training speed. ALBERT achieves state-of-the-art results on GLUE, RACE, and SQuAD benchmarks while using 18x fewer parameters than BERT-large.
title: ALBERT: A Lite BERT for Self-supervised Learning

text: DistilBERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter. DistilBERT is trained by distilling BERT base using knowledge distillation during pretraining. It has 40% fewer parameters, runs 60% faster, and retains 97% of BERT's language understanding capabilities and 60% faster.
title: DistilBERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter

text: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining. XLNet is a generalized autoregressive pretraining method that enables learning bidirectional contexts by maximizing the expected likelihood over all permutations of the factorization order during training. XLNet outperforms BERT on 20 tasks including SQuAD 2.0, NaturalQuestions, GLUE.
title: XLNet: Generalized Autoregressive Pretraining

text: GPT-2: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners. GPT-2 with 1.5B parameters demonstrates that language models begin to learn NLP tasks without explicit supervision when trained on WebText, 8 million web pages. The model achieves state-of-the-art zero-shot performance on 7 out of 8 tested language modeling datasets.
title: GPT-2: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners

text: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners. GPT-3 with 175B parameters achieves strong few-shot performance on many NLP tasks, sometimes rivaling fine-tuned models. In-context learning with just a few examples enables strong results on translation, question-answering, cloze tasks, and several tasks requiring on-the-fly reasoning.
title: GPT-3: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

text: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models. LLaMA models from 7B to 65B parameters are trained on publicly available data only. LLaMA-13B outperforms GPT-3 on most benchmarks despite being 10x smaller. LLaMA-65B is competitive with Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B.
title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models

text: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models. Llama 2 pretrained and fine-tuned LLMs from 7B to 70B parameters. Llama 2-Chat is optimized for dialogue using RLHF with over 1 million human annotations. Llama 2-Chat outperforms open-source chat models and is on par with some closed-source models on human evaluations.
title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models

text: Mistral 7B. Mistral 7B outperforms Llama 2 13B on all benchmarks and Llama 1 34B on many benchmarks. It uses grouped-query attention for faster inference and sliding window attention to handle sequences of arbitrary length with no memory overhead.
title: Mistral 7B

text: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways. PaLM is a 540B parameter dense decoder-only Transformer model trained using Pathways on 780B tokens. PaLM achieves breakthrough performance on 28 of 29 NLP tasks, demonstrates few-shot chain-of-thought reasoning capabilities, and shows exceptional multilingual performance.
title: PaLM: Scaling Language Modeling with Pathways

text: Chinchilla: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models. Chinchilla scaling laws show current LLMs are significantly undertrained. For compute-optimal training, model size and training tokens should be scaled equally. Chinchilla 70B trained on 1.4T tokens outperforms Gopher 280B, GPT-3 175B, and PaLM 540B despite using the same compute budget as Gopher.
title: Chinchilla: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models

text: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models. LoRA freezes pretrained model weights and injects trainable rank decomposition matrices into each Transformer layer. This reduces trainable parameters by 10000x and GPU memory by 3x compared to fine-tuning. LoRA matches or outperforms fine-tuning on GPT-3 and GPT-2 with no additional inference latency.
title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models

text: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs. QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen 4-bit quantized pretrained LLM into Low Rank Adapters. QLoRA reduces memory enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning performance. The resulting Guanaco model outperforms previous openly released models on the Vicuna benchmark.
title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs

text: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation. Prefix-tuning prepends a sequence of continuous task-specific vectors to the input and keeps LM parameters frozen while optimizing only the prefix. Prefix-tuning with 0.1% of parameters matches fine-tuning on table-to-text and summarization in full-data settings and outperforms fine-tuning in low-data settings.
title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation

text: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning. Prompt tuning conditions frozen language models with a small number of learned soft prompt tokens prepended to the input. At the scale of T5-XXL, prompt tuning matches the strong performance of model tuning while being much more parameter-efficient. Soft prompts are learned through backpropagation over a labeled training set.
title: The Power of Scale for Parameter-Efficient Prompt Tuning

text: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP. Adapters add small bottleneck layers to each transformer layer and only train these adapter layers during fine-tuning, keeping the pretrained model frozen. Adapters achieve near state-of-the-art performance on GLUE with only 3.6% additional parameters per task.
title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP

text: InstructGPT: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback. InstructGPT fine-tunes GPT-3 with RLHF using a dataset of human-written demonstrations and comparisons. A reward model trained on human comparisons is used as the reward signal in PPO training. InstructGPT is preferred over GPT-3 by labelers despite having 100x fewer parameters.
title: InstructGPT: Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback

text: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model. DPO shows that the RLHF objective can be optimized exactly with a simple cross-entropy loss on preference data without reward modeling or RL. DPO is more stable, computationally lighter, and produces similar or better performance compared to RLHF with PPO on summarization and dialogue.
title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model

text: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback. Constitutional AI trains harmless AI assistants through self-improvement using a list of principles called a constitution. The AI generates responses, critiques them according to the constitution, and revises them. The final RL step uses AI-generated feedback instead of human feedback labels.
title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback

text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks. RAG combines parametric memory from a pretrained seq2seq model with non-parametric memory from a dense passage retriever. The retriever finds relevant documents and the generator produces the final answer conditioned on both the input and retrieved documents. RAG achieves state-of-the-art on Open NQ, WebQ and CuratedTrec.
title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks

text: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering. DPR uses two independent BERT encoders for queries and passages and trains them with in-batch negative sampling. DPR outperforms BM25 by 9-19% exact match accuracy on NQ, TriviaQA, WebQ, and CuratedTrec, while being trained on only 1000 examples for some datasets.
title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

text: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Late Interaction. ColBERT uses late interaction: independently encode query and document with BERT, then compute relevance via a cheap MaxSim operation over all token embeddings. ColBERT is 170x faster than BERT cross-encoder re-rankers while achieving comparable MRR@10 on MS MARCO.
title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Late Interaction

text: Sparse, Dense, and Attentional Representations for Text Retrieval. Hybrid retrieval combining sparse BM25 and dense embeddings consistently outperforms either alone across diverse retrieval tasks. Linear interpolation of BM25 and dense scores with a fixed weight achieves strong performance. The paper motivates adaptive weighting per query.
title: Sparse, Dense, and Attentional Representations for Text Retrieval

text: Blended RAG: Improving RAG Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers. Blended RAG combines BM25, KNN dense vectors, and ELSER sparse semantic encoder via hybrid query strategies (Best Fields, Cross Fields, Phrase Prefix). Blended RAG achieves NDCG@10=0.87 on TREC-COVID and 0.67 on NQ, outperforming all prior benchmarks including COCO-DR and monoT5-3B.
title: Blended RAG: Improving RAG Accuracy with Semantic Search and Hybrid Query-Based Retrievers

text: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection. Self-RAG trains an LLM to adaptively retrieve passages and generate text interleaved with special reflection tokens for retrieval, relevance, support and utility. Self-RAG outperforms ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-Chat on open-domain QA, reasoning, and fact verification.
title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection

text: HyDE: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels. HyDE instructs an LLM to generate a hypothetical document for the query, then uses an encoder to embed this hypothetical document for retrieval. Despite being unreal, the hypothetical document captures relevance patterns and dramatically improves zero-shot dense retrieval performance.
title: HyDE: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels

text: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval. RAPTOR recursively embeds, clusters, and summarizes chunks of text building a tree with different levels of abstraction. At inference time it retrieves from this tree integrating information across lengthy documents at different levels. RAPTOR significantly outperforms chunk-based RAG on QASPER and NarrativeQA.
title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval

text: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented LLMs through Question Complexity. Adaptive-RAG trains a small classifier to predict query complexity and route queries to the appropriate retrieval strategy: no retrieval, single-step retrieval, or multi-step retrieval. This achieves better performance and efficiency than always using the most complex strategy.
title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented LLMs through Question Complexity

text: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks. SBERT uses siamese and triplet network structures with BERT to produce fixed-size sentence embeddings. SBERT reduces the time for finding the most similar pair from 65 hours with BERT to 5 seconds while maintaining accuracy. SBERT sets new state-of-the-art on semantic textual similarity benchmarks.
title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks

text: BGE M3-Embedding: Multi-Lingual Multi-Functionality Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings. M3-Embedding supports 100+ languages and unifies dense retrieval, lexical retrieval, and multi-vector retrieval in a single model trained with self-knowledge distillation. M3 achieves state-of-the-art on BEIR and MIRACL benchmarks.
title: BGE M3-Embedding: Multi-Lingual Multi-Functionality Multi-Granularity Text Embeddings

text: E5: Text Embeddings by Weakly-Supervised Contrastive Pre-training. E5 uses weakly supervised contrastive pretraining on curated web text pairs without expensive labeled data. E5 outperforms models trained on labeled datasets on both BEIR and MTEB benchmarks. Fine-tuned E5-large achieves the best overall performance on MTEB.
title: E5: Text Embeddings by Weakly-Supervised Contrastive Pre-training

text: FAISS: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs. FAISS provides efficient similarity search for dense vectors including IndexFlatL2, IndexIVFFlat, and IndexHNSWFlat. GPU FAISS achieves billion-scale nearest-neighbor search in one second. FAISS is widely used in recommendation systems, visual search, and retrieval augmented generation pipelines.
title: FAISS: Billion-scale similarity search with GPUs

text: HNSW: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search. HNSW builds a multilayer graph structure where each node is connected to its nearest neighbors at different scales. Search navigates from coarse to fine layers. HNSW outperforms all existing ANN methods on recall-performance tradeoff for all query scales.
title: HNSW: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search

text: BM25: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework. BM25 ranks documents by the sum of IDF-weighted term frequency scores with saturation and document length normalization. BM25 is a strong baseline for information retrieval that consistently outperforms TF-IDF and is used as the default ranker in Elasticsearch and Lucene search engines.
title: BM25: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework

text: SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Retrieval. SPLADE learns sparse representations by applying a log-saturation over BERT token representations with max-pooling, producing bag-of-words style sparse vectors. SPLADE achieves state-of-the-art retrieval on MS MARCO while matching BM25 efficiency through an inverted index.
title: SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Retrieval

text: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text. SQuAD contains 100,000+ crowdsourced question-answer pairs on 500+ Wikipedia articles where answers are text spans. SQuAD v2 adds 50,000 unanswerable questions. SQuAD is the standard benchmark for reading comprehension and question answering research.
title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text

text: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research. Natural Questions consists of 307,373 Google search queries paired with Wikipedia pages containing long and short answer annotations. NQ tests the ability to retrieve and read evidence from Wikipedia to answer naturally occurring questions.
title: Natural Questions: A Benchmark for Question Answering Research

text: HotpotQA: Multi-hop Question Answering. HotpotQA contains 113K Wikipedia-based questions requiring multi-hop reasoning over multiple documents with supporting fact supervision. It tests two reasoning strategies: bridge questions requiring chaining two documents and comparison questions requiring comparing two entities.
title: HotpotQA: Multi-hop Question Answering

text: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of IR Models. BEIR contains 18 diverse retrieval datasets covering bio-medical, financial, scientific, and general domains. BM25 is a surprisingly strong baseline, outperforming many neural models in zero-shot settings, motivating domain-specific fine-tuning of retrieval models.
title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of IR Models

text: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models. Chain-of-thought prompting provides a series of intermediate reasoning steps as few-shot examples to elicit multi-step reasoning. CoT is an emergent ability appearing only in models above 100B parameters. CoT prompting significantly improves arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning.
title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

text: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning. Self-consistency samples a diverse set of reasoning paths and selects the most consistent final answer by majority voting. Self-consistency significantly improves CoT prompting performance on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning, outperforming greedy decoding by large margins.
title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning

text: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs. Tree of Thoughts generalizes CoT to allow exploration of multiple reasoning paths, self-evaluation of intermediate thoughts, and lookahead or backtracking. ToT achieves 74% on Game of 24 where CoT achieves only 4%, and significantly improves creative writing.
title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with LLMs

text: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models. ReAct interleaves reasoning traces and task-specific actions, allowing the model to dynamically retrieve information and update its plan. ReAct outperforms chain-of-thought on HotpotQA and FEVER, and outperforms imitation and reinforcement learning on interactive decision tasks.
title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

text: CLIP: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision. CLIP trains a vision encoder and text encoder jointly to predict which caption matches which image using a contrastive objective on 400M image-text pairs. CLIP achieves zero-shot transfer competitive with supervised baselines on ImageNet and 30 other datasets.
title: CLIP: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision

text: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Vision Transformer. ViT applies a standard Transformer to sequences of image patches for image classification. When pre-trained on large datasets, ViT attains excellent results on ImageNet, CIFAR-100, and VTAB while requiring substantially fewer computational resources than CNNs to train.
title: An Image is Worth 16x16 Words: Vision Transformer

text: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning. Flamingo bridges pretrained vision-only and language-only models with cross-attention layers. Flamingo achieves state-of-the-art few-shot performance on 16 multimodal benchmarks including VQA, COCO captioning, and video QA by conditioning on arbitrarily interleaved images and text.
title: Flamingo: a Visual Language Model for Few-Shot Learning

text: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning. LLaVA connects CLIP visual encoder with LLaMA using a simple linear projection and trains on GPT-4 generated multimodal instruction-following data. LLaVA-1.5 achieves state-of-the-art on 11 benchmarks using only public data.
title: LLaVA: Visual Instruction Tuning

text: Knowledge Distillation: A Survey. Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a large teacher model to a small student model through soft probability targets, intermediate feature matching, or attention transfer. Applications include model compression, cross-modal learning, and continual learning.
title: Knowledge Distillation: A Survey

text: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for NLU. TinyBERT introduces transformer distillation with attention matrix distillation and value relation distillation. TinyBERT-4L has 7.5x fewer parameters and is 9.4x faster than BERT-base while achieving 96.8% of BERT performance on GLUE.
title: TinyBERT: Distilling BERT for NLU

text: Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts. The Sparsely-Gated MoE layer routes each input to the top-k of N expert networks using a learnable gating network. MoE increases model capacity 1000x with only minor computational overhead by using sparse activation. MoE achieves state-of-the-art on WMT En-Fr translation.
title: Sparsely-Gated Mixture-of-Experts

text: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models. Switch Transformer simplifies MoE by routing each token to exactly one expert. This reduces communication costs and achieves 7x faster pretraining speed than T5 at the same FLOP count. Switch Transformers scale to 1.6 trillion parameters.
title: Switch Transformers: Scaling to Trillion Parameter Models

text: Mixtral of Experts. Mixtral 8x7B uses 8 experts per MoE layer with top-2 routing, accessing only 13B active parameters out of 47B total. Mixtral matches or outperforms Llama 2 70B and GPT-3.5 on most benchmarks while being 6x faster at inference.
title: Mixtral of Experts

text: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models. Neural language model performance scales as power-laws with model size, dataset size, and compute budget, spanning 7 orders of magnitude. For a fixed compute budget, larger models trained on less data outperform smaller models trained longer. These laws inform optimal resource allocation.
title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models

text: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models. Emergent abilities appear abruptly when model scale crosses certain thresholds, not present in smaller models. Examples include multi-step arithmetic, taking exams, and explaining jokes. Emergence motivates continued scaling of language models.
title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models

text: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision. FActScore breaks generated text into atomic facts and measures the percentage supported by a reliable knowledge source. FActScore better correlates with human factuality judgments than existing metrics. Current LLMs achieve only 58.4% FActScore on biography generation.
title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision

text: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods. TruthfulQA contains 817 questions designed to elicit common misconceptions. GPT-3 is truthful on only 58% of questions while humans achieve 94%. Larger models tend to be less truthful, imitating falsehoods in pretraining data. RLHF substantially improves truthfulness.
title: TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods

text: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation. Hallucination in NLG includes intrinsic contradictions of source content and extrinsic unverifiable claims. Key causes are exposure bias, copy mechanism errors, and parametric knowledge conflicts. Mitigation strategies include retrieval augmentation, constrained decoding, and RLHF.
title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation

text: YOLO: You Only Look Once: Unified Real-Time Object Detection. YOLO frames object detection as regression to bounding boxes and class probabilities from a single neural network pass. YOLO processes images at 45 FPS with 63.4 mAP on PASCAL VOC, compared to 7 FPS for DPM and 18 FPS for Fast RCNN while achieving comparable accuracy.
title: YOLO: You Only Look Once: Unified Real-Time Object Detection

text: DETR: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers. DETR uses a Transformer encoder-decoder with bipartite matching loss to directly predict a set of object detections, eliminating NMS and anchor generation. DETR achieves 42.0 AP on COCO, matching Faster RCNN with fewer parameters and strong performance on large objects.
title: DETR: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers

text: Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Classification. GCN propagates features through a graph using a simple layer-wise rule motivated by first-order spectral graph convolutions. GCN achieves state-of-the-art on semi-supervised node classification on Cora, Citeseer, and Pubmed citation networks with only a fraction of labeled nodes.
title: Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Classification

text: Graph Attention Networks. GAT computes node representations by attending over neighborhoods with learnable attention weights that do not require knowledge of the graph structure. GAT achieves state-of-the-art on Cora, Citeseer, Pubmed, and the inductive PPI dataset.
title: Graph Attention Networks

text: Codex: Evaluating LLMs Trained on Code. Codex is GPT fine-tuned on 100B tokens of public GitHub code. On HumanEval, a new benchmark of 164 Python programming problems, Codex solves 28.8% using a single sample and 70.2% using 100 samples. GPT-3 solves 0% on HumanEval.
title: Codex: Evaluating LLMs Trained on Code

text: CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages. CodeBERT is bimodal BERT pretrained on 8.35M code-documentation pairs from GitHub in 6 programming languages. CodeBERT achieves state-of-the-art on code search, code documentation generation, and code-to-code search tasks.
title: CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages

text: Neural Machine Translation with Subword Units (BPE). Byte-pair encoding learns a variable-length subword vocabulary by iteratively merging the most frequent symbol pairs. BPE enables open-vocabulary NMT and reduces out-of-vocabulary rates. BPE improves BLEU by 1.1-11.8 on WMT translation tasks.
title: Neural Machine Translation with Subword Units (BPE)

text: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models: A Survey. This survey covers additive methods (adapters, prefix tuning, prompt tuning), selective methods (BitFit, DiffPruning), reparameterization methods (LoRA, IA3), and hybrid methods. PEFT methods achieve comparable performance to full fine-tuning with 0.1-3% of parameters updated.
title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models: A Survey

text: SimCLR: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning. SimCLR applies contrastive loss to representations after a nonlinear projection head using augmentations including random cropping, color distortion, and Gaussian blur. SimCLR achieves 76.5% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet with ResNet-50, outperforming previous self-supervised methods by 7%.
title: SimCLR: A Simple Framework for Contrastive Learning

text: FedAvg: Communication-Efficient Learning from Decentralized Data. FedAvg performs multiple local SGD steps on each client before averaging model weights on the server. FedAvg reduces communication rounds by 10-100x over synchronous SGD while achieving similar accuracy on image classification and language modeling tasks.
title: FedAvg: Communication-Efficient Learning from Decentralized Data

text: T5: Exploring Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer. T5 converts every NLP task into text-to-text format and pre-trains with a span-corruption objective on the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus. T5-11B achieves state-of-the-art on GLUE, SuperGLUE, SQuAD, CNN-DM, and WMT translation benchmarks.
title: T5: Exploring Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer

text: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training. BART pre-trains a standard sequence-to-sequence Transformer by learning to reconstruct text from corrupted input using token masking, deletion, infilling, permutation and rotation. BART achieves state-of-the-art on summarization, dialogue, and abstractive QA.
title: BART: Denoising Sequence-to-Sequence Pre-training

text: Passage Re-ranking with BERT. Cross-encoder BERT re-ranker concatenates query and passage and fine-tunes on MS MARCO click labels. BERT re-ranker achieves MRR@10 of 0.365 on MS MARCO dev vs 0.167 for BM25. A two-stage BM25+BERT pipeline achieves 0.358 MRR@10 efficiently.
title: Passage Re-ranking with BERT

text: Query Rewriting for Retrieval-Augmented LLMs. Rewrite-Retrieve-Read uses an LLM to rewrite user queries to be more specific before retrieval. The rewritten query leads to more relevant retrieved documents and better final answers. Query rewriting improves performance on open-domain QA by up to 12% accuracy.
title: Query Rewriting for Retrieval-Augmented LLMs

text: FLARE: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation. FLARE iteratively predicts upcoming sentences, retrieves if low-probability tokens appear, and regenerates with retrieved documents as context. FLARE outperforms standard RAG and RETRO on long-form generation tasks including open-domain QA and fact completion.
title: FLARE: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation

text: Graph RAG: Query-Focused Summarization over Document Corpora. Graph RAG extracts an entity knowledge graph from source documents using an LLM, generates community summaries at multiple granularities, and answers queries by combining global and local context. Graph RAG significantly outperforms standard RAG on sensemaking queries.
title: Graph RAG: Query-Focused Summarization over Document Corpora

text: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark for NLU. GLUE includes 9 sentence or sentence-pair tasks covering NLI, similarity, sentiment, QA, and linguistic acceptability. Human baseline is 87.1. BERT achieves 80.4 while GPT achieves 72.8. GLUE motivates multi-task learning and general NLU models.
title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark for NLU

text: MMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding. MMLU covers 57 subjects from STEM to humanities with 14K multiple choice questions. GPT-3 few-shot achieves 43.9% while expert human performance is around 89%. MMLU reveals that LLMs have large knowledge gaps in specialized domains.
title: MMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding

text: IA3: Few-Shot PEFT is Better and Cheaper than ICL. IA3 rescales activations by learned vectors that are injected into attention and feedforward layers. IA3 adds only 0.01% additional parameters and outperforms full fine-tuning in few-shot settings while being more efficient than in-context learning at inference time.
title: IA3: Few-Shot PEFT is Better and Cheaper than ICL

text: Universal Sentence Encoder. Universal Sentence Encoder trains sentence encoders with a multi-task learning framework including NLI and response prediction. The transformer variant achieves stronger transfer performance on STS, SICK, and several classification tasks compared to averaging word embeddings.
title: Universal Sentence Encoder

text: StarCoder: May the Source Be With You!. StarCoder is a 15.5B parameter code LLM trained on 80+ programming languages from The Stack dataset. StarCoder achieves state-of-the-art on HumanEval, MBPP, and DS-1000, matching or outperforming GPT-3.5 on Python while being open-source.
title: StarCoder: May the Source Be With You!

text: kNN-LM: Nearest Neighbor Language Models. kNN-LM interpolates a neural LM distribution with a nearest-neighbor distribution retrieved from a datastore of cached context-target pairs. kNN-LM improves perplexity across multiple domains without additional training and enables effective domain adaptation by swapping the datastore.
title: kNN-LM: Nearest Neighbor Language Models

text: INSTRUCTOR: One Embedder Any Task. INSTRUCTOR generates task-specific embeddings by prepending task instructions to input text and training with a contrastive objective on 330 diverse tasks. INSTRUCTOR achieves state-of-the-art on MTEB without task-specific fine-tuning.
title: INSTRUCTOR: One Embedder Any Task

text: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization. Overoptimization of proxy reward models occurs as KL divergence from the initial policy increases. The gold reward first increases then decreases as optimization continues. Larger proxy reward models and larger initial policies are more robust to overoptimization.
title: Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization

text: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Feedback. This paper provides a unified theoretical view of RLHF and DPO as special cases of a general framework. Identity Preference Optimization IPO directly minimizes the KL-regularized objective without reward modeling and is more stable than DPO.
title: A General Theoretical Paradigm to Understand Learning from Human Feedback

text: CRAG: Comprehensive RAG Benchmark. CRAG contains 4409 QA pairs spanning 5 domains with web search and knowledge graph APIs. The best RAG model achieves only 34% accuracy versus 89% for humans, showing that grounded generation remains a major challenge even with retrieval.
title: CRAG: Comprehensive RAG Benchmark

text: Lost in the Middle: How LLMs Use Long Contexts. LLMs perform best when relevant information appears at the beginning or end of contexts but significantly worse when it appears in the middle. Performance degrades as context length increases. This motivates better retrieval to surface relevant information prominently.
title: Lost in the Middle: How LLMs Use Long Contexts

text: Neural Approaches to Conversational Information Retrieval. This survey covers neural re-ranking from early learning-to-rank approaches to modern cross-encoder re-rankers. Cross-encoders consistently outperform bi-encoders for re-ranking but are slower. Two-stage retrieve-then-rerank pipelines balance efficiency and effectiveness.
title: Neural Approaches to Conversational Information Retrieval
